hook_text: A dome of sticks you could snap over your knee stands through a storm. The people who built it had no hardware shop and did not need one.
clip_script: Zulu beehive hut: saplings pushed into the ground, bent over, lashed into a dome, one of the strongest shapes there is, because every push runs round the curve to the ground. Thatch laid bottom up so water steps from layer to layer, tied down with a grass net. Low door, dung floor. Rondavel: woven walls plastered in mud and dung, thick enough to hold the day's heat for the night, under a thatched cone that sheds rain every way and overhangs the wall. Nama matjieshuis: a dome of sticks under rush mats that breathe in the heat and swell shut in the rain, moved on an ox in a day. All of it from a few kilometres away, and all of it goes back to the earth. One honest weakness: thatch burns. So do not copy the hut. Borrow the dome, the overlaps, the overhang, the tie-down, the mound, and the builders.
visual_style: Whiteboard dome of arcs with hoops; thatch layers stacking bottom up; a cone over a cylinder with overhanging eaves; a rolled mat on an ox; a short borrow list.
mood: Admiring and analytical, learning from the land.
pacing: Dome, thatch, rondavel, mats, source, weakness, borrow, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list what your shelter can borrow from a hut.
